summary: Lisa Grumbach works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She held posts at Stanford University (attested 1996) and as an assistant professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Lisa N. Owen specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. She earned her M.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Texas at Austin by 2006 under Janice Leoshko, and studied under Walter M. Spink in 1995.
Lita Peipina is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned an MA at the University of Oslo (attested 2008). She studied under Jens Braarvig in 2003 and also studied under Jens-Uwe Hartmann.

Lloyd W. Pflueger works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He earned his doctorate at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and served as Professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University (attested 2015).

Lobsang Dargyay (1935–1994) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rahor Monastery, Drepung Monastery (~1952–1959), and earned a Dr.phil. at the University of Munich (~1971–1974).

Lobsang Gyatso (1928–1997) studied at Drepung Monastery (~1940–1959) and under Tendzin Chökyi Gyatso. A scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he founded and headed the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics (~1973–1997) and founded the College for Higher Tibetan Studies.

Lobsang Jamspal (born 1936) is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Columbia University under Alex Wayman. He held posts at Sampurnanand, Delhi, CIHTS, and on the Columbia faculty (attested 1985–1990).
Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa (1926–2008) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Dudjom Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, among other teachers.

Lobsang Shastri specializes in Tibetology. He served as Head Librarian at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (attested 2003–2006) and as Senior Librarian at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (attested 2018).

Lobsang Tenpa works in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history and archaeology. He completed a Master of Philosophy at Jawaharlal Nehru University under the supervision of Sharad K. Soni.

Lobsang Tenzin (born 1939) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He held positions at the Central Schools for Tibetans in Shimla (1961), Darjeeling (1964), and elsewhere (1965–1970), and directed CIHTS (~1988–2000).

Lobsang Yongdan works in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Kumbum Monastery and earned a PhD at the University of Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger, later holding postdoctoral posts at MPIWG and the University of Bonn.

Loden Sherab Dagyab (born 1940) studied at Drepung Monastery and under Tenzin Gyatso. Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he directed Tibet House, New Delhi (1964–1966), served as a Tibetologist at Bonn (1966), and founded Tibethaus Deutschland.
Lodrö Chökyi Sengé studied under Kalu Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and also taught Kalu Rinpoche.

Lodrö Sangpo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Ernst Steinkellner. He founded the Nitartha Institute in 1996 and served as a senior teacher at Gampo Abbey (attested 2008).

Lokesh Chandra (1927–2022) studied at Punjab University and Utrecht under Jan Gonda. A scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, he was Secretary (~1950–1963) and Director (~1963–2022) of the IAIC, and chaired ICCR and ICHR.
Longlian (1909–2006) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Fazun in 1939 and Nenghai Shi from circa 1941 to 1967.

Lore Sander (1936–2023) studied Indology, Buddhist studies, and Central Asian studies under Ernst Waldschmidt. She curated at the Museum of Asian Art (1987) and held posts at the universities of Hamburg, Berlin, Munich, and Free University Berlin.

Lori Meeks earned a BA from Columbia and a PhD from Princeton under Jacqueline I. Stone. Working in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, she held posts at Stanford (~2003–2004) and the University of Southern California (~2004).

Lorna Dewaraja (1929–2014) studied at the University of Ceylon and University of London. In history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, she served at the University of Peradeniya (~1957–1978), University of Colombo (~1978–1989), and St Anne's College.
